chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who travels during the month of Ramadan and with him is a slave girl, and whether it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her during the day. He said: 'Glory be to Allah! Does he not recognize the sanctity of the month of Ramadan? For him, during the night, is a long duration.'

I said, 'Is it not for him that he can eat, drink, and shorten (the prayer)?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has granted concession to the traveler regarding breaking the fast and shortening (the prayer) as a mercy and alleviation for the place of fatigue, exertion, and difficulty of travel. But He did not grant him concession regarding intercourse with women during the day while traveling in the month of Ramadan. He obligated upon him making up the fasts, and did not obligate upon him making up the complete prayers when he returns from his journey.'

Then he said: 'And the Sunnah cannot be measured by analogy, and I, whenever I travel during the month of Ramadan, do not eat except for the bare necessities, and do not drink until I quench my thirst completely.'
ai.seo_question: Can a traveler have sexual intercourse during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general concession for travelers to break the fast and shorten prayers and the specific prohibition of sexual intercourse during Ramadan days, emphasizing that the latter is not covered by the travel exemption. He highlights the sanctity of Ramadan nights ('sabhan tawilan') and illustrates the superior etiquette (adab) of the Sunnah, where the Prophet minimized consumption to mere sustenance rather than full satisfaction, distinguishing legal permissibility from spiritual excellence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who travels during a Month of Ramazan and with his is a slave girl. Is it for him that he attains from her in the daytime?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Does he not recognise the sanctity of a Month of Ramazan? For him, during the night, is a lengthy duration’.

I said, ‘Is it not for him that he can eat and drink and shorten (the Prayer)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Allowed for the traveler regarding the breaking (of the Fast), and the shortening (of the Prayer), as a Mercy and a lightening due to the fatigue, and the setting up (of tents etc.), and moths of the travel, but He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Allow for him regarding the sleeping with the women by the day, during the journey, in a Month of Ramazan, and Obligated upon him the making up for the Fasts and did not Obligate upon him the making up for the complete when he returns from his journey’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the Sunnah cannot be analogized, and I<sup>asws</sup>, whenever I<sup>asws</sup> travel during a Month of Ramazan, do not eat except for the bare necessities, and do not drink for the whole thirst’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who travels in the month of Ramadan and with him there is his slave-girl: if he can experience sexual relation with her during the day in the month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah is free of all defects. Does he not recognize any respect for the month of Ramadan and that during the night there is a long time for him?’

I then asked, ‘Can he not eat, drink and reduce his Salat (prayer)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Blessed, most High, has granted permission to stop fasting and reduce one’s Salat (prayer) while on a journey. It is as a mercy and to provide ease for him; he becomes tired because of the difficulties of traveling. He has not granted permission to have sexual relation with a woman on a journey during the day in the month of Ramadan. He has made Qada’ (compensatory fast) of the fast of the month of Ramadan obligatory on him but He has not made Qada’ (compensatory) Salat (prayer) in complete form obligatory when he returns from his journey.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘It is not permissible to measure the Sunnah by means of analogy. When I travel in the month of Ramadan I do not eat more than bare necessities and do not drink to completely quench my thirst.’”
